_match_name: Exemption from Tuition Fees for International Students under the Heidelberg University Charter of 28 July 2017

official.application_cycle: Recurring twice-yearly cycle with fixed recurring deadlines; as at 2026-10-03 the winter semester 2026/27 round closed on 15 July 2026 and the next round, for the summer semester 2027, closes on 15 January 2027
official.deadline_central_display: "15 July for the following winter semester / 15 January for the following summer semester (date of receipt)" - both are exclusion deadlines (Ausschlussfrist)
official.deadline_note: The official sources publish only the recurring month and day (15 July for the winter semester, 15 January for the summer semester), never an exact calendar year-specific date, so deadline_date and deadline_central are null and deadline_precision is "varies". No time of day is published; the rule is receipt by the university, so Europe/Berlin is used as the institution's local timezone rather than as a published value. The most recent past deadline was 15 July 2026 for winter semester 2026/27; the next opportunity is 15 January 2027 for the summer semester 2027. Both dates fall on the last day of the corresponding re-registration window (15 June to 15 July for the winter semester, 15 January to 15 February for the summer semester). University notice: a deadline ending on a Sunday, Saturday or public holiday is NOT extended to the next working day (Section 31 paragraph 3 sentence 2 and paragraph 5 Landesverwaltungsverfahrensgesetz Baden-Wuerttemberg). deadline_institutional records the last past cycle date, 15 July 2026.
official.status_note: The winter semester 2026/27 application round closed on 15 July 2026, before the verification date of 2026-10-03, so the current cycle is closed. The scheme itself is a standing entitlement with no intake limit: the next round, for the summer semester 2027, closes on 15 January 2027, and the following winter semester 2027/28 round closes on 15 July 2027. Decisions on the summer semester round are notified in March 2027, and on the winter semester round in August.
official.funding_duration: For the standard period of study (Regelstudienzeit) of the enrolled degree programme; the charter states no fixed number of years. A six-semester bachelor's programme carries EUR 9,000 in international tuition fees at EUR 1,500 per semester.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The award is a tuition-fee waiver only, so tuition_coverage is true, but fully_funded is false. The exemption covers only the EUR 1,500 per semester Baden-Wuerttemberg international tuition fee and may be granted only in part. It does not cover the mandatory semester contribution, which the university states separately as EUR 189.80 per semester (as of the 2026/27 winter semester), and it covers no living cost at all. International students must independently evidence funds of at least EUR 992 per month for visa purposes as of summer semester 2026, and the university estimates about EUR 35,700 for a six-semester bachelor's programme excluding tuition fees, so a tuition waiver alone must not be presented as funding a study programme.
official.funding_label: Heidelberg University tuition-fee exemption - EUR 1,500 per semester, full or partial, for the standard period of study; semester contribution of EUR 189.80 and all living costs remain payable
benefits: Full or partial exemption from the EUR 1,500 per semester international tuition fee for Bachelor's and Staatsexamen programmes
Normally granted for the standard period of study of the enrolled degree programme
No cash stipend, no accommodation, no travel and no insurance benefit
Decided by the Central Admission Committee of the Senate for International Students
eligibility: Be a fee-liable international student under Section 2 LHGebG: not a citizen of an EU or EEA member state and holding a foreign university entrance qualification
EU/EEA nationals and holders of a German university entrance qualification are exempt from the fee and cannot apply for this waiver
Be enrolled, or about to enrol, in an undergraduate or Master's degree programme at Heidelberg University at the start of the approval period
Prove special aptitude (besondere Begabung) under Section 4 of the charter
Submit a separate written application in the prescribed form with all evidence attached
Have the application received by 15 July for the winter semester or 15 January for the summer semester
Finance living costs independently
official.citizenship_residency: Restricted to students who are liable for the Baden-Wuerttemberg international tuition fee, i.e. nationals of countries outside the EU and EEA (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway) who hold a foreign university entrance qualification. EU and EEA nationals and students with a German university entrance qualification are exempt from the fee under state law and are therefore not eligible. The official English pages consulted name only EU and EEA and do not mention Swiss nationals.
official.international_eligibility: International applicants from outside the EU/EEA who hold a foreign university entrance qualification and who are admitted to, or about to enrol in, an undergraduate degree programme at Heidelberg University. No nationality quota is published, but the charter directs particular consideration to students from African, Caribbean and Pacific states and from least-developed countries.
official.application_method: Separate application required - the waiver is not granted automatically on admission. Submit the official form "Application for exemption from tuition fees for international students in accordance with the Heidelberg University charter of 28 July 2017", signed, scanned with all evidence and emailed (preferably PDF) to studiengebuehren@zuv.uni-heidelberg.de so that it is received by 15 July for the winter semester or 15 January for the summer semester. If the admission application period for the chosen programme closes earlier, the exemption application may be sent together with the admission application. Documents must be in German or English; translations must be by a sworn or officially authorised translator with stamp and signature. Fee collection is handled electronically and notifications are sent electronically.

The only published language rule is a document-language rule: application documents must be in German or English, and any translations must be prepared by a sworn or officially authorised translator bearing stamp and signature.

supplements_or_initiatives: Two separate Heidelberg routes exist for international students and are not this award: statutory exemptions under Section 5 LHGebG and hardship waivers under Section 7 LHGebG or Section 22 (2) LGebG. The Section 7 hardship waiver is expressly not open to students taking up their studies for the first time in a first-semester degree or partial degree programme

The waiver is one instrument under Section 6 (4) LHGebG, under which Baden-Wuerttemberg universities may exempt up to 5% of international first-semester students fully or partially on grounds of special aptitude
Heidelberg University publishes a separate scholarship opportunities page pointing applicants to external bodies such as DAAD, since it offers very few scholarships of its own

official.description: Baden-Wuerttemberg charges international students from non-EU/EEA countries with a foreign university entrance qualification a tuition fee of EUR 1,500 per semester for Bachelor's and Staatsexamen programmes. Heidelberg University uses the statutory 5% quota to waive that fee for up to a Rectorate-set number of international students per semester, on evidence of special aptitude. Applications are made separately from admission, on the university's official form, and must be received by 15 July for the winter semester or 15 January for the summer semester. Successful applicants are exempted for the standard period of study of their programme, and the semester contribution and all living costs remain payable.
official.coverage: The exemption covers the EUR 1,500 per semester international tuition fee only, in full or in part. It does not cover the EUR 189.80 semester contribution, living costs, housing, travel or insurance.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are actually fee-liable: you are a non-EU/EEA national with a foreign university entrance qualification. If you hold a German university entrance qualification or an EU/EEA passport, you already pay no tuition fee and must not apply.

Secure your admission offer or enrolment certificate for the undergraduate programme first - it is a mandatory attachment and you must be enrolled, or about to enrol, at the start of the approval period.

Assemble evidence of special aptitude: school or academic results beyond the normal Abitur grade, performance-based distinctions, or prizes and scholarships. At least one of the three charter routes must be documented.
Download the official form "Application for exemption from tuition fees for international students in accordance with the Heidelberg University charter of 28 July 2017" and complete both pages.
Have translations ready - documents must be German or English, and any translation needs a sworn or officially authorised translator with stamp and signature.
If you are claiming social circumstances, write the separate explanation of at most two DIN A4 pages.
Email the signed scan as PDF to studiengebuehren@zuv.uni-heidelberg.de early, targeting receipt well before 15 January or 15 July.
Do your own funding plan in parallel: the waiver touches tuition only, and you must still evidence EUR 992 per month for the visa.
common_rejection_risks: Missing the exclusion deadline - 15 July for the winter semester and 15 January for the summer semester are Ausschlussfrist and are not extendable if they fall on a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday.
Assuming admission is enough - the waiver needs its own application and is never granted automatically.
Applying as an EU/EEA national or holder of a German university entrance qualification, which makes the applicant ineligible because the fee does not apply to them.
Omitting the admission or enrolment proof, which the charter makes a mandatory attachment.
Submitting generic evidence without mapping it to one of the three Section 4 routes, so that special aptitude is not established.
Leaving the social-circumstances explanation out while relying on social criteria, which the charter only allows once explained.
Assuming a full waiver - the committee may grant only a partial exemption, decided under Section 5 of the charter.
Sending documents in a language other than German or English, or using uncertified translations.
estimated_uncovered_costs: The semester contribution of EUR 189.80 per semester (2026/27 winter semester), which the university states remains obligatory even where a tuition waiver is granted
All living costs: the university estimates about EUR 35,700 for a six-semester bachelor's programme excluding tuition fees
Visa and residence permit costs
Rent: approximately EUR 350 in student housing to EUR 950 on the private market
Food: approximately EUR 200 to EUR 400 per month
Health insurance: approximately EUR 150 per month, rising to about EUR 300 for those over 30
Public transport: approximately EUR 45 to EUR 63 per month
Leisure, clothing and study materials: approximately EUR 150 to EUR 300 per month
Up-front costs on arrival such as furnishing an apartment and a deposit
Travel to and from Germany

alerts.message: Heidelberg may exempt only up to 5% of international first-semester students, and the Rectorate sets the actual number per semester. A strong application can still miss the quota, and the committee may award a partial rather than a full exemption.
The waiver is not automatic on admission. Enrol without an approved exemption and you remain liable for EUR 1,500 per semester.

15 January and 15 July are exclusion deadlines under Section 2 (1) of the charter. Per Baden-Wuerttemberg administrative law they are not extended when they fall on a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday.
The waiver removes the tuition fee only. The EUR 189.80 semester contribution and your entire living budget stay with you, and the visa still requires proof of about EUR 992 per month.
After 15 July 2026 the next chance is 15 January 2027 for the summer semester 2027, with a decision notified in March 2027.

False or negligently supplied information is treated as an administrative offence and leads to exclusion or to revocation of an existing exemption, and the exemption lapses on subject change, dropout or deregistration.

submission_workflow: Apply for admission to the undergraduate degree programme and obtain the admission offer.
Check that you are fee-liable under Section 2 LHGebG before spending effort on the application.
Gather evidence of special aptitude under Section 4 of the charter.
Download and complete the official exemption form.
Scan the signed form and all evidence, get any required certified translations.
Email everything as PDF to studiengebuehren@zuv.uni-heidelberg.de so it is received by 15 January for the summer semester or 15 July for the winter semester.
If the programme's admission deadline falls earlier, send the exemption application together with the admission application and expect a decision after the general deadline.
Watch for the electronic notification - decisions arrive in March for the summer semester and August for the winter semester.

unverified_or_removed_claims: No exact calendar deadline date is published anywhere: the official sources give only the recurring 15 July and 15 January, so deadline_date and deadline_central are null by design.
No time of day and no explicit timezone are published; Europe/Berlin is inferred from receipt at a German university.
The actual per-semester exemption quota set by the Rectorate is not published on the pages read; only the statutory ceiling of up to 5% of international first-semester students is stated.

Swiss nationals are not named on the English pages read. State law exempts them from the fee, which would make them ineligible for this waiver, but the pages consulted do not confirm this and it is not recorded as a fact.
No English language test requirement or score is published for the waiver; only a German-or-English document language rule exists.
No published numerical selection weighting exists between the aptitude, social and equality criteria.
No fixed number of years is published for the exemption, because the charter ties it to the standard period of study of each individual programme.

The study-financing page warns that international students cannot normally cover these costs with part-time work, and notes there are very few scholarships in Germany; it does not quantify what is left after a waiver and no such figure is derived here.

The tuition fee exemption is confirmed to apply to Bachelor's and Staatsexamen programmes; the charter text also covers consecutive Master's programmes, but no separate bachelor's-only rule was published.

official.application_cycle: 2026-27 admission cycle for entry in autumn 2027; the Common Application opens in early August 2026 and the cycle closes with the Early Decision admission deadline on November 2, 2026. The 2026-27 CSS Profile becomes available to complete online by October 1, 2026.

Regular Decision: admission January 4, 2027; CSS Profile February 1, 2027. deadline_central records the soonest closing date, the Early Decision admission deadline of November 2, 2026. deadline_institutional is null because no Duke institutional date falls EARLIER than November 2, 2026 - Duke's own financial aid dates (November 3 and February 1) both fall after their paired admission dates. One inconsistency on Duke's own site is recorded rather than resolved: the Apply and Checklist pages list "Financial Aid Applications - CSS Profile, FAFSA" under November 2, while the Financial Support page and its international-applicant panel both state November 3. November 3 is used because the Financial Support page is the page that owns the aid deadlines. official.status_note: Open as of 2026-10-03. The Common Application has been available since early August 2026, the 2026-27 CSS Profile is available to complete online by October 1, 2026, and the next closing date is the Early Decision admission deadline of November 2, 2026 with the CSS Profile due November 3, 2026. official.funding_duration: Four years of full-time undergraduate study. Duke states its merit scholarships "cover the cost of tuition, mandatory fees, room, and board for four years of full-time undergraduate studies", and the Karsh award additionally includes three summers of funding.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Tuition is covered in full, and the award does not stop at the cost of attendance. Duke's own published answer to "What does it cover?" is: "Your tuition, room and board, mandatory fees, demonstrated need that exceeds those costs, and three summers of funding for research, unpaid internships, and other opportunities that will advance your academic career." The Karsh Office of Undergraduate Financial Support states "Duke meets 100% of demonstrated need for undergrads." Because the coverage explicitly extends to demonstrated need in excess of tuition, room and board and mandatory fees, tuition_coverage is true and fully_funded is true. THE SAME STATEMENT MAKES THE AWARD CONDITIONAL: the award is need-based and the documented-need condition is mandatory. Duke states "International applicants must have demonstrated financial need to be eligible for this scholarship", and the published candidate profile is "Strong academic preparation and documented need for financial aid." The documented need is established through the CSS Profile and, on request, translated foreign tax documents. There is no award without documented financial need, so fully_funded describes the ceiling of the package for a holder who has documented need, not an unconditional entitlement. Not published as covered: international airfare, US visa and I-901 SEVIS fees - Duke's 2026-27 cost of attendance lists only "Transportation (domestic) $582-$1,318, depending on home address".
official.funding_label: Need-based full package with no fixed published figure: covers tuition, room and board, mandatory fees, demonstrated need exceeding those costs, and three summers of funding for research and unpaid internships. Duke's 2026-27 first-year cost of attendance before aid is tuition $73,740, estimated fees $3,019 (plus $60 Engineering Dues for Pratt students), housing (double room) $11,560 and food $10,469, total billed $98,788-$98,848, total cost of attendance $103,180-$103,975. Award size is set from documented need against that cost of attendance, not from a fixed amount.

official.citizenship_residency: Open to citizens of any country outside the United States. Candidates with dual U.S./other-country citizenship cannot be considered. U.S. citizens, permanent residents and undocumented or DACA applicants are routed through Duke's domestic need-based aid process and international transfer applicants are excluded from need-based aid entirely. Duke publishes no separate home-country tuition rule.
official.international_eligibility: "Can a student who is a citizen of any country outside the U.S. be considered for this scholarship? Yes." International applicants who indicate interest in financial aid are considered in a separate, more competitive admission pool, and Duke states the admit rate for foreign citizens seeking financial aid is usually less than half of the overall admit rate. Duke issues four-year aid awards for international applicants, automatically renewed for subsequent years, and requires attendance at a financial aid session on arrival for the aid to be applied.
official.study_mode: Full-time undergraduate study at Duke University
official.application_method: Automatic on admission, with a separate financial aid application. There is no separate Karsh application and no nomination: "Please note that to apply for the Karsh Scholarship, you must apply to Duke University and request financial aid. There is no separate application." The applicant submits the Duke undergraduate admission application, indicates interest in financial aid, submits the 2026-27 CSS Profile through the College Board, submits the FAFSA where applicable, and responds to any additional-documentation request through the College Board's IDOC service. Finalists for merit scholarships are notified by email from OUSF in the spring, interview with scholarship selection committees, and the award is made shortly after the interviews.

official.english_requirement: Not required. Duke recommends but does not require an English proficiency test and has no preference among tests. Published minimum scores expected: TOEFL 100 internet-based or 75 revised paper-delivered (including TOEFL Home Edition); IELTS 7; PTE Academic 70; Duolingo English Test 130; Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency 180.
official.english_requirement_note: Duke states: "If you are a non-native English speaker or if you are not currently studying in an English-medium curriculum, we recommend but do not require that you take an English proficiency test. If you take the test more than once, we will use your highest score, and we do not have any preference among English proficiency tests." Because official submissions of the Duolingo English Test are free, Duke suggests an official submission of those results, while all other English proficiency scores may be self-reported. These are Duke's admission-side English expectations; the Karsh page itself publishes no separate English requirement.

official.description: Duke University's Karsh International Scholarship was founded in 2010 through a generous donation from Martha L. and Bruce A. Karsh and recognises the outstanding potential for academic and global impact of international students. Karsh International Scholars comprise an intellectually and civically engaged cohort who promote interdisciplinary inquiry, academic research and scholarship in the service of society. The award is need-based: international applicants must have demonstrated financial need to be eligible. Duke states it covers tuition, room and board, mandatory fees, demonstrated need that exceeds those costs, and three summers of funding for research, unpaid internships and other opportunities that will advance the student's academic career. There is no separate application; the Duke undergraduate admission application is the basis on which eligibility is determined.
official.coverage: Tuition, room and board, mandatory fees, demonstrated need exceeding those costs, and three summers of funding for research, unpaid internships and other opportunities that advance the student's academic career. official.description: The Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarships are the University of Toronto's most prestigious award for international students and, by the university's own description, one of the largest scholarship programmes for international students in Canada, with scholars drawn from 188 countries. They cover tuition, books, incidental fees and full residence support for four years, are tenable only at the University of Toronto for first-entry undergraduate programs, and name approximately 37 Scholars each year; the university publishes a programme-level figure of $12M+ funding in 2024 but no per-scholar dollar amount. Reaching the award requires three sequential steps: nomination by the student's high school, which may nominate only one student per year, by October 9, 2026; an OUAC admission application by October 16, 2026; and a separate scholarship application with all required documentation by November 6, 2026. Eligibility is restricted to non-Canadians requiring a study permit who are in the final year of senior secondary school in 2026/2027 or graduated no earlier than June 2026 and who begin studies in September 2027. The university publishes an explicit fraud warning: it does not interact with educational agents or agencies to recruit students or offer scholarships, and recipients can only be nominated by their current secondary school through the online process.
official.coverage: Tuition, books, incidental fees and full residence support for four years at the University of Toronto, tenable only for first-entry undergraduate programs. No travel, study-permit or personal-expense component is published. Published residence fees on future.utoronto.ca/housing give scale context only: Innis College Residence $13,645 per Academic Year with no required meal plan, CampusOne Residence $30,380 to $37,848 per 12-month lease including a required meal plan.

application_readiness_checklist: Ask your guidance counsellor, principal or head of school this term whether your school is already verified for the Pearson programme — this is the single gate on the whole application and it closes first.

If your school is not yet verified, submit the school's application to participate at https://apply.adm.utoronto.ca/register/pearson-participate; the published cut-off is noon (EST) on October 9, 2026, which is earlier than most families expect.

Submit your OUAC application for admission to at least one undergraduate U of T program by October 16, 2026, not by the general January 15, 2027 deadline, or you will not be considered for the scholarship.
Watch your inbox for the private Pearson Scholarship application link; it is issued after your school nominates you, and the form cannot be completed before your admission application is submitted.

Have your final-year results, predicted grades and any IB/AP/A-Level documentation ready to upload, because the scholarship documentation deadline of November 6, 2026 falls before most 2027 admission decisions.
Book any required English proficiency test early and register it with your name exactly as it appears on your OUAC application — the university cannot match results if names or dates of birth differ.
Plan the three dates on one calendar now: October 9 (nomination), October 16 (OUAC), November 6 (scholarship application and documents). They run school-first, then admission, then scholarship.
Arrange study-permit and Provincial Attestation Letter timing for a September 2027 start; the PAL is issued by the university only after you accept the offer and pay the admission deposit.
Start assembling reference-free personal material — the university has banned generative AI from award applications, so anything you write for the scholarship form must be entirely your own.
common_rejection_risks: Missed the school nomination deadline of October 9, 2026 — the award cannot be reached without a nomination, and this date is roughly five weeks before the scholarship application deadline.
Applying to U of T by the general January 15, 2027 deadline instead of October 16, 2026, which removes you from Pearson consideration even if you are admitted.
Submitting the scholarship form before your OUAC admission application; the page states the form can be completed only after the admission application has been submitted.
Starting post-secondary study in January 2027 rather than September 2027, which the university names explicitly as disqualifying.
Already being in post-secondary study at the time of application, which is also named as disqualifying.
Being a Canadian citizen, permanent resident or protected person; the award is reserved for non-Canadians requiring a study permit.
Using generative AI to draft any part of the scholarship application, which the university says results in disqualification from award eligibility.
Paying an agent who promises a nomination or a scholarship offer — the university publishes no agent channel and warns against exactly this.
Restricting the scholarship to a lower-choice program: the award is bound to your top-choice program at the time scholarship decisions are made.
Missing supporting-document deadlines for the admission application itself, which run from December 1 for early applicants to February 1 depending on program area.
estimated_uncovered_costs: No per-scholar dollar value is published, so the award cannot be converted into a budget line. Build your plan around the four named components plus the published residence fee scale: Innis College Residence $13,645 per Academic Year (no required meal plan), CampusOne Residence $30,380 to $37,848 per 12-month lease (required meal plan included), Knox College Residence $17,898 to $19,585 per Academic Year.
Airfare and travel to Canada are not named in the published package.
Study-permit and Provincial Attestation Letter government fees are not named in the published package.
Personal living expenses beyond residence, including any non-included meals, are not named in the published package.
Any award paid to a student who is not admitted, or who accepts a place at another institution, is not addressed in the published terms.
Books are covered, but the page does not state whether any print or course-material surcharge is included.
U of T states separately that it is a publicly funded institution and cannot offer financial aid to international students, so nothing outside the four published components should be assumed.
document_audit: The public Pearson page sets the documentation deadline but does not enumerate the scholarship application's own attachments — download the list from your private application link and treat that list, not this record, as authoritative.
Match the name and date of birth on your English test registration exactly to your OUAC application, or the university says it cannot match the results to your file.

Confirm your English test is on the accepted list and is the right sitting: IELTS Academic (not Indicator, not One Skill Retake), TOEFL iBT (not MyBest, Essentials, ITP or ITP Plus for China), PTE Academic, Duolingo, CAEL, Cambridge C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency, IB English, CXC English, GCSE/IGCSE/GCE/AICE English or an accepted alternative qualification.

If you sit TOEFL iBT before 21 January 2026 the thresholds are the older scale (total 89 with 22 in each of Speaking and Writing); after that date they are 4.5 overall with 4.5 Writing and 4.0 Speaking. Do not mix scales across tests.
Have notarized translations ready for every document not already in English or French, since the university requires them and this is a common late-stage delay.
Official transcripts must be sent directly by the issuing institution at any point in the process, even if you uploaded an unofficial copy for a provisional decision.
Keep your school nomination confirmation: with one nominee allowed per school, proof of nomination is the only thing separating a complete file from an incomplete one.
Do not submit identical AI-generated prose to the scholarship form and to any other award application; the prohibition covers all U of T undergraduate award applications.

official.description: The Vice Chancellor's International Scholarship is a competitive Griffith University tuition-fee award for international students. It reduces tuition fees by 50% for the duration of the degree, for candidates commencing undergraduate or postgraduate coursework programs in 2026 or 2027 who hold a Letter of Offer, are citizens of countries other than Australia or New Zealand, hold a GPA of at least 6.0 on a 7-point scale, and enrol full-time. The reduction is applied before the census date of each trimester; the remaining balance is payable by the student. Continuation depends on maintaining a cumulative GPA of at least 5.5 on a 7.0 scale, and the amount is non-refundable if the student withdraws. There is no bond or service obligation, and no living, accommodation or travel component.

official.description: The K.C. Kuok Scholarship is a Monash University award funded and named after alumnus Khoon Chen Kuok, better known as Beau Kuok, which supports financially disadvantaged students to complete a full-time undergraduate degree at any of Monash's Australian campuses. One scholarship is available in 2026 for commencement in February 2027, and Monash states a total value of up to AUD 360,000 over four years covering tuition fees, a AUD 14,000 per year allowance, accommodation at Monash University Accommodation, student visa costs, a AUD 3,000 one-off establishment payment and the first incoming flight to Australia. It is open to citizens of mainland China, Indonesia, Hong Kong and Southeast Asia who have not yet commenced university study at any institution and can demonstrate that they come from a low income household.
official.coverage: Full tuition fees for the duration of a single full-time undergraduate degree; AUD 14,000 per year living allowance; accommodation at Monash University Accommodation paid directly to the provider for the course duration, limited to standard residential contract periods and excluding summer accommodation fees; student visa costs; an AUD 3,000 one-off establishment payment in the first year; and the first incoming flight to Australia in the first year.

official.description: The Science & Technology Undergraduate Scholarship is a freshmen scholarship offered to support outstanding Asian students (excluding Singapore citizens), considered and shortlisted through the applicant's application for undergraduate admission to NUS. It provides 100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant, a S$6,000 annual living allowance, an annual accommodation allowance equivalent to the lowest double room rate for on-campus accommodation, a one-time S$1,750 computer allowance, a one-time S$200 settling-in allowance, and a travel allowance for incoming and return passage. It is tenable for the normal candidature period of the programme, renewed each semester subject to a GPA of at least 3.50 and good conduct, and recipients must serve a six-year bond with a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation.

_match_name: Bourse du Gouvernement Français (French Government Scholarship)

official.application_cycle: Annual cycle; each French embassy or consulate abroad publishes its own call and deadline for the academic year it is awarding. No single central application window exists.
official.deadline_central_display: No central deadline. The ministry states: "Quel que soit leur pays de résidence, les candidats doivent donc, avant leur départ et suffisamment à l'avance, s'adresser directement à ces services situés dans leurs pays d'origine afin d'obtenir toutes les informations sur ces bourses : conditions d'attribution, calendrier de sélection, dossiers à constituer." Deadlines therefore close per country, set by the awarding embassy or consulate.
official.deadline_note: There is deliberately no central deadline. The Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs states that the majority of these scholarships are awarded by the cultural cooperation services of French embassies and consulates abroad, and that candidates must contact those services in their country of origin to obtain the attribution conditions, the selection calendar and the documents to assemble. The deadline_precision is therefore 'varies'. The only exact dates published centrally are admission dates for a Licence programme, which are a separate procedure and not the scholarship deadline.
official.status_note: The scheme is a standing annual programme rather than a single call with one deadline. Embassy and consulate calls open and close on their own national calendars, so the award is neither simply open nor simply closed on any single date. Verified against the ministry page last updated 5 August 2026.
official.funding_duration: Awarded for a fixed period tied to the programme, the course and the institution; the rate applies for the duration of the scholarship.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Tuition is covered only in part and only by exemption, not by payment. Campus France states that a French government scholarship holder, on presenting its scholarship or financial-support certificate, 'will be exempted from' paying the CVEC and from 'the payment of enrolment fees relating to pursuing a national degree or an engineering degree in public scientific, cultural, and professional establishments under the authority of the Minister for Higher Education' (Article R719-49 of the Education Code). Two limits are stated on the same page: the exemption does not extend to training fees ('Campus France does not cover the education fees and you are responsible for them') and Campus France does not reimburse enrolment or tuition fees already paid to the institution. fully_funded is therefore false: there are uncovered components (training fees, housing rent, most day-to-day living costs) and binding scholarship-holder obligations.
official.funding_label: French Government Scholarship (Bourse du Gouvernement Français) - EUR 900 per month at Licence (bachelor's) level, EUR 900 at Master's, EUR 1,850 at doctoral level; CVEC and public-sector national-degree enrolment fees exempted; holder must attend the programme, sit all exams and report to Campus France, and travel is only covered where the ministry or embassy funds it.

official.citizenship_residency: Open to foreign students only, excluding French nationals. official.international_eligibility: Explicitly for international (foreign) students studying in France. The ministry describes the scheme as 'les bourses du gouvernement français' allocated 'pour des études, des stages ou des séjours linguistiques en France', awarded by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs.

official.application_method: A separate application, not automatic on admission. The scholarship is applied for directly to the French embassy or consulate (Service de coopération et d'action culturelle) in the candidate's country of residence, which sets the conditions and the selection calendar. Admission to a French programme is a separate procedure: first-year Licence applications go through the national 'Etudes en France' platform at pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr, where applications open on 1 October 2026 and close on 15 December 2026 for the entry year, with university responses before 30 April 2027.

official.description: The Bourse du Gouvernement Français is the umbrella status for French government scholarships awarded by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs for study, internship and language stays in France. The majority are awarded by the cultural cooperation services of French embassies and consulates abroad rather than in Paris, so the Licence track is applied for and decided country by country. Campus France implements the awarded scholarship and publishes the official rate grid: EUR 900 per month for a Licence or Master's level scholarship and EUR 1,850 per month for a doctoral one. Holders are exempted from the CVEC and from enrolment fees for national and engineering degrees in public establishments under the Minister for Higher Education, but training fees and most living costs stay with the holder, and the status carries binding attendance, examination and reporting obligations.
official.coverage: Covers a monthly maintenance allowance of EUR 900 at Licence level (EUR 1,850 at doctoral level), exemption from the CVEC and from public-sector national-degree enrolment fees, social security affiliation with up to two months of interim cover, and air travel only where the ministry or the awarding embassy funds it. It does not cover training fees, housing rent or most day-to-day living costs.

official.description: The President's International Distinction Scholarship is the University of Alberta's most prestigious and competitive scholarship for international students. Each year 25 students with a superior admission average and demonstrated leadership qualities entering their first year of an undergraduate degree on a student visa permit receive up to CAN $120,000, payable over four years. It is an application-based award: applicants must first apply to an undergraduate degree program, then submit the University's single scholarship application by January 10, and offers are made starting in early winter. The University of Alberta states that it does not offer full scholarships for either domestic or international students, so the award funds part rather than all of the cost of an international degree.
official.coverage: Cash scholarship of up to CAN $120,000 payable over four years, to 25 recipients per year. Not a full-cost award. The University of Alberta's International Tuition + Fees page identifies the four cost components of an international degree - instructional tuition fees, non-instructional fees, books and supplies, and living arrangement - none of which is separately covered by this award.

official.description: The Tasmanian Aurora Excellence Scholarship is the University of Tasmania's most selective academic-merit award for commencing international students, providing a 50% reduction in registered tuition fees for the duration of the course, credited to the student's account after each census date. Eligible courses include all undergraduate bachelor and honours coursework programs apart from a named exclusion list, so the award is funded at bachelor's level as well as postgraduate. Applications are invitation-triggered: the University invites applicants who hold an offer and are eligible for the Tasmanian International Merit Scholarship, and sends a link to the scholarship application form. Assessment uses a 90 ATAR or equivalent threshold, the application form, a 300-500 word personal statement and an interview for shortlisted candidates. The benefit is tuition only and is capped at five years full-time equivalent; the Terms and Conditions expressly exclude the Student Services and Amenity Fee, accommodation, insurance, books and other non-tuition costs, and the scholarship is neither redeemable for cash nor transferable.
official.coverage: Covers 50% of published international tuition fees for the standard duration of the eligible course, up to five years full-time equivalent. Does not cover the Student Services and Amenity Fee, accommodation, insurance, books, repeated units, units beyond course requirements, or any travel or living costs.

The University's international scholarships index page lists the Tasmanian Aurora Excellence Scholarship under the heading "Scholarships that you will be automatically assessed for" and states generally "For many of our International Scholarships, you will be assessed at the time of submitting your International Student Application so there is no need to apply separately." Applications for the scholarship are open from 27 July 2026 and close on 1 October 2027, and the scholarship is awarded for study commencing in 2027 or 2028 at a Curtin Western Australian campus. official.deadline_note: This is the scholarship's own published closing date and it is exact: 1 October 2027, Australia/Perth (AWST, UTC+8). No time of day is published, so deadline_precision is 'day'. Two caveats are recorded rather than resolved. First, Curtin reserves the right to cease offering the Scholarship when all Scholarship places are filled, so the published date is not a guarantee that a place remains. Second, because assessment is automatic on the Curtin course application, the binding constraint for any individual applicant is the course application closing date for the chosen intake, which differs by course and by intake. official.description: The John Curtin Global Excellence Scholarship is a merit-based scholarship funded by Curtin University. Eligible students receive 40% off the tuition fee of the course they are undertaking, credited for up to 4 years for an undergraduate degree course or a maximum of 2 years for a Master degree by coursework, as a tuition fee credit against all units enrolled within the course within the scholarship term. It is open to international, fee-paying, non-sponsored students of any nationality except Australian who will study at a Curtin Western Australian campus commencing in 2027 or 2028, and who have achieved a Course-Weighted Average of 95% or equivalent in their most recent and eligible course of study. The scholarship is credited to the recipient's fee account after the census date of the first study period, only covers tuition fees, and cannot be withdrawn or refunded in cash. There is no separate scholarship application: all qualifying applications to Curtin are assessed automatically and Global Admissions confirms the outcome by issuing a supplementary letter with the Letter of Offer.
official.coverage: 40% of the tuition fee of the course, credited for up to 4 years for an undergraduate degree course or a maximum of 2 years for a Master degree by coursework. Tuition fees only; no living cost, accommodation, travel or other international student expense is covered.

official.tuition_coverage_note: The published benefit is '100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees (after MOE Tuition Grant - scholarship recipients must take up the MOE Tuition Grant)'. Two limitations keep fully_funded false. First, the coverage is of subsidised tuition fees only and is calculated after the MOE Tuition Grant, so any non-subsidised component and any compulsory ancillary, laboratory or miscellaneous fee is not stated to be covered. Second, and decisively, the coverage is conditional on accepting the MOE Tuition Grant, which for international students carries a 3-year bond to work for a Singapore-registered company immediately upon graduation; MOE confirms independently that 'Tuition Grant recipients who are Singapore Permanent Residents or international students must serve a 3-year bond after graduation.' An unavoidable service obligation means the record cannot be represented as fully funded.

official.description: The ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship is an SMU-administered undergraduate award from Singapore Management University for applicants who are citizens of ASEAN member countries other than Singapore and who are applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at SMU. SMU publishes 100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant, an annual living allowance of S$5,800, an annual accommodation allowance of S$3,000 and a one-time computer allowance of S$1,750 on enrolment. The scholarship carries no bond of its own, but because the tuition coverage is conditional on accepting the MOE Tuition Grant, every international recipient is placed under the Ministry of Education's 3-year bond to work for a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation. Recipients must keep a cumulative GPA of 3.0 out of 4.0 at the end of every academic term, may take at most one term of overseas programme outside the final year, and must repay liquidated damages if they breach the terms.
official.coverage: Subsidised undergraduate tuition fees in full after the MOE Tuition Grant, plus an annual living allowance of S$5,800, an annual accommodation allowance of S$3,000 and a one-time computer allowance of S$1,750. alerts.trigger: Evaluating this award as full funding
alerts.message: SMU publishes 100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees but only after the MOE Tuition Grant, and that grant carries a 3-year bond to work for a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation, with only full-time employment counting. Price the bond into any comparison rather than reading this as cost-free study.

SMU publishes no separate scholarship closing date. The award follows the undergraduate admission timeline, whose published closing date for international and other qualifications was 19 March 2026, 11.59pm, Singapore Standard Time for the AY2026-27 intake. Next-cycle dates were not published when this record was verified on 2026-10-03, so treat the deadline as variable rather than fixed.

The published cycle ran from mid-November to mid-March, shortlisted applicants attend an interview or test between March and May, and outcomes are released in batches from May to July. An application submitted after the closing date cannot be considered for the scholarship.

alerts.trigger: Test score deadline trails the application deadline
alerts.message: For AY2026-27 the application closed on 19 March 2026 but the standardised test score was due by 31 March 2026. Missing the second date after applying is an easy, avoidable loss.

alerts.trigger: Checking for a 75 per cent credits rule
alerts.message: The condition that at least 75% of graduation credits be earned in Singapore appears in the ASEAN scholarship terms of other Singapore universities, but SMU's own page does not state it. SMU publishes only that overseas programmes of up to one term are allowed and not in the final year. Confirm the credits position with SMU before assuming either rule.
The scholarship still applies to Double Degree Programmes only if both degrees are completed within the standard four-year student tenure.

submission_workflow: 1. Confirm ASEAN citizenship other than Singapore citizenship and check your qualification against SMU's list of accepted international qualifications.
2. Sit one accepted standardised test if you do not already hold one, and register for the electronic score send.
3. Complete the SMU online application for admission for a full-time undergraduate degree programme.

4. In the Scholarship section of that application, indicate interest in the ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship. There is no separate scholarship form, so an application that omits this is not considered.
5. Upload standardised test scores via Applicant's Self Service and submit the application before the published closing date, with the test score by its own later deadline.
6. Submit through the Applicant's Self Service Portal as the scholarship page requires.
7. If shortlisted, attend the interview or, for Law, the writing test.
8. If offered the scholarship and admission, accept the MOE Tuition Grant as part of the offer, since the tuition coverage depends on it.
9. On enrolment, keep the CGPA at or above 3.0 out of 4.0 in every academic term, avoid taking an overseas programme in the final year, and do not accept a concurrent award without written approval.

official.description: The International Student Merit Scholarship is a Charles Sturt University tuition-fee reduction for new commencing international students, valued at a 25% fee discount for the entire duration of the course and deducted from tuition fees at the commencement of each session. It is awarded automatically by the admissions team when an applicant applies for an approved course in internal/on-campus mode at an eligible campus, with no separate application process, and the outcome is advised with the offer letter. Academic entry is assessed either through an Australian AQF Level 7 progression route or through published Year 12 equivalent thresholds of 75 per cent for most undergraduate degrees and 85 per cent for Allied Health courses other than Nursing. There is no bond, no living-cost component and no travel component.
official.coverage: Covers a 25% reduction in tuition fees for the entire duration of the course, deducted from tuition fees at the commencement of each session. Does not cover the remaining 75% of tuition, accommodation, living costs, travel, visa or the e-COE, and no bond attaches to the award.

application_readiness_checklist: Pick your course from CSU's published list of approved courses and check the entry-score threshold attached to it before you apply: 75 per cent Year 12 equivalent for most undergraduate degrees, 85 per cent for Allied Health except Nursing.

Apply to an approved course in internal/on-campus mode at Albury-Wodonga, Bathurst, Dubbo, Melbourne, Orange, Port Macquarie, Sydney or Wagga Wagga. Do not rely on an online-mode offer, which is expressly ineligible.
No separate scholarship form exists. Your CSU admission application is the scholarship application, so do not spend time hunting for a scholarship portal.

If you are relying on the Australian academic progression route, have your AQF Level 7 or above completion certificate and date ready, and make sure the completion date is within 12 months of your course commencement date.
Keep the offer letter, because the scholarship decision travels with it, and pay the fee deposit promptly so the e-COE is issued.
Budget for the remaining 75% of tuition plus accommodation, living costs, travel and visa yourself: this award is a fee discount, not a funded place.
Read the promotional conditions before you accept: you will be expected to join the student body, give testimonials, be photographed, and sign a media release.
Do not accept another Charles Sturt-funded tuition fee scholarship alongside this one, and do not assume it can be combined with a CSU-funded award.
common_rejection_risks: Applying for an online-mode course, which is expressly excluded from the scholarship even though CSU offers online degrees.
Applying through a CSU international partner rather than to a CSU campus, which is also excluded.
Missing the academic entry threshold for the specific approved course, where Allied Health and most other undergraduate degrees carry different thresholds.

Being a continuing student, or transferring from another CSU course or applying with advanced standing without confirming eligibility first; the page excludes transferring students while noting that some advanced-standing cases are still treated as commencing.
Holding an Australia Awards or Research Training Program scholarship, which disqualifies the applicant from this award.
Submitting through an exchange or study abroad channel rather than a degree admission.
Accepting a second CSU-funded tuition fee scholarship, which terminates eligibility for this one.
Missing the 11:59pm 31 Dec 2026 cut-off, since assessment runs through the admissions process and late offers may fall outside the published window.

official.description: The SUTD Trailblazers (International) Scholarship is a Singapore University of Technology and Design tuition award for high-performing incoming undergraduates who are Singapore Permanent Residents or international students. It covers the subsidised tuition fees, after the Singapore Government Tuition Grant, for the normal duration of the relevant bachelor's degree programme, up to four years. Applicants must apply for the scholarship at the same time as their SUTD admission application, are shortlisted, and are then considered in competition by a selection committee whose decision is final. Recipients must take up the Tuition Grant Scheme to enjoy the subsidised rate, must maintain good academic standing reviewed every term, must complete at least 20 hours of service to the University, may not hold other awards without approval, and are exposed to a case-by-case repayment if they terminate the scholarship prematurely.

_match_name: University of Ljubljana Tuition Fee Exemption for International Students

official.application_cycle: Not an application cycle. The exemption is a standing rule for full-time study, and the University republishes the exemption conditions and the tuition and study-contribution price lists each academic year; the price lists on the page are for academic year 2026/2027.
official.deadline_central_display: No application deadline is published. The University states the exemption applies to "full-time bachelor's and master's studies" and publishes no opening date, closing date or call for applications for it.
official.deadline_note: There is no application window to record, so deadline_central, deadline_central_timezone and deadline_institutional are all null. The exemption is not applied for on a deadline; it is settled when the student enrols in full-time study, and the University publishes the rule rather than a call. Enrolment deadlines for foreign nationals from non-EU member states exist as a separate published Call for Enrolment, but that call governs admission, not this exemption, and it was not fetched, so no date and no timezone are claimed. Any such University of Ljubljana deadline would fall in Europe/Ljubljana time, but no published time was read, so the field stays null.
official.status_note: Continuously in force for full-time study; the University published the current conditions and the 2026/2027 price lists at the time of verification on 2026-10-03. There is no open or closed window because there is no application. The exemption is periodically revised by statute and the fee amounts are reissued every academic year, so the status refers to the standing rule, not to a cycle that can close.
official.funding_duration: For the duration of the student's full-time study for as long as the exemption conditions are met, carried forward through enrolment each academic year; the University publishes no fixed award term.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Covers the tuition fee in full for full-time bachelor's and master's study, and nothing else. It does not cover enrolment fees and study contributions, compulsory health insurance, accommodation, living costs, study materials or travel, and it carries no cash payment. The University lists all part-time students among those obliged to pay tuition fees, so the exemption is void for part-time enrolment. It is also lost by exempt students who change study programme or direction and enrol in the same or a lower study year after already having exercised the right to repeat a year, and by exempt students who re-enrol in the same study programme or direction from which they previously withdrew, as both groups are expressly listed as obliged to pay. Because the award is tuition-only and leaves the remaining components of the cost of study payable, fully_funded is false.
official.funding_label: Full tuition fee waived for full-time study; enrolment fees and study contributions, health insurance, accommodation and living costs all remain payable by the student. No stipend, no cash amount, no bond or service obligation.
benefits: Tuition fee waived in full for full-time bachelor's or master's study while the exemption conditions are met
Available without an application, a selection round or a competition
Recognised across all University of Ljubljana member institutions for fee purposes, with the fee amount published separately per faculty or academy
eligibility: Slovenian citizens, including Slovenians living outside the borders of the Republic of Slovenia and persons without Slovenian citizenship as defined by the relevant law

Exchange students, including doctoral exchange students
Full-time study only; all part-time students are obliged to pay
Not eligible: citizens of non-EU countries with which the Republic of Slovenia has not signed a bilateral agreement
Not eligible: students who already hold an equivalent degree of education
official.citizenship_residency: Determined by nationality, residence status and protection status rather than by merit. The University lists Slovenians (including those abroad and those without Slovenian citizenship as defined by the relevant law), citizens of EU countries plus Switzerland, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway, nationals of Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Serbia under bilateral education agreements, permanent residents of the Republic of Slovenia who are taxpayers of the Republic of Slovenia, persons granted international protection and persons under temporary protection, Republic of Slovenia scholarship holders and exchange students. Citizens of non-EU countries with which the Republic of Slovenia has not signed a bilateral agreement are expressly listed as obliged to pay.
official.international_eligibility: For the group this record is aimed at, the University publishes no open international scholarship competition: the only international schemes it runs are the Residency of Prof. Grega Košak, a 4.5-month residency for artists, designers, restorers, theorists and researchers from around the world, and the Heart UL campaign for enrolled students in financial emergency, neither of which funds a bachelor's degree's tuition. Non-EEA nationals of Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Serbia qualify for the tuition exemption through a bilateral education agreement with the Republic of Slovenia, and persons granted international protection or under temporary protection qualify irrespective of nationality; all other non-EEA nationals are listed as paying. Scholarships linked from the University's page for international students, such as the Zois scholarships and the various open calls, are awarded by the Public Scholarship, Development, Disability and Maintenance Fund of the Republic of Slovenia and are not University of Ljubljana awards.
official.study_mode: Full-time only; the University lists all part-time students among those obliged to pay tuition fees.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field, subject or faculty restriction on the exemption itself. The amount is field-specific: the University publishes one 2026/2027 price list per member institution (Academy of Fine Arts and Design, Academy of Music, Academy of Theatre Radio Film and Television, Biotechnical Faculty, Faculty of Architecture, Arts, Chemistry and Chemical Technology, Civil and Geodetic Engineering, Computer and Information Science, Education, Electrical Engineering, Health Sciences, Law, Maritime Studies and Transport, Mathematics and Physics, Mechanical Engineering, Medicine, Natural Sciences and Engineering, Pharmacy, Public Administration, Social Sciences, Social Work, Sport, Theology, School of Economics and Business and Veterinary Faculty), plus a separate price list for enrolment fees and study contributions, a separate list for interdisciplinary bachelor degree programmes, a separate list for interdisciplinary and joint master's programmes, a separate doctoral tuition list and a separate set of general conditions for the payment of tuition fees. Doctoral study is explicitly outside the exemption.
official.application_method: Automatic on enrolment. The University publishes the exemption as a standing fee rule, so there is no separate application, no application form, no call and no selection process; the exemption is applied in the ordinary course of enrolment.
official.application_route: No separate application route. The exemption is applied for in the course of enrolling in full-time study at the University of Ljubljana member institution in which the student studies, under the rules published on the University tuition fees page; the University's Higher Education Application and Information Service handles enrolment.

selection_criteria: No selection criteria. The exemption is a standing tuition-fee rule applied by nationality, residence status, protection status, prior degree and study mode, not a competitive award, and the University publishes no shortlist, ranking or interview.

Residency of Prof. Grega Košak: a University of Ljubljana residency of four and a half months in an apartment in the centre of Ljubljana for artists, designers, restorers, theorists and researchers from around the world. It is a residency, not a degree scholarship, and does not fund a bachelor's programme.

State scholarships for international students listed on the University page, including Zois scholarships and various open calls, are administered and awarded by the Public Scholarship, Development, Disability and Maintenance Fund of the Republic of Slovenia (srips-rs.si), not by the University; the University states that the Fund publishes the open call defining all requirements, procedures and the amount of scholarship grants.
Republic of Slovenia scholarship holders, including CMEPIUS holders, are listed by the University as exempt from tuition fees, so a state scholarship can also remove the tuition fee for the holder.

official.description: A statutory tuition-fee exemption applied by the University of Ljubljana, not a competitive scholarship. Full-time bachelor's and master's study is fee-free for Slovenians (including Slovenians abroad and persons without Slovenian citizenship as defined by the relevant law), citizens of EU countries plus Switzerland, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway, nationals of Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Serbia under bilateral education agreements, permanent residents of the Republic of Slovenia who are taxpayers, persons granted international protection or under temporary protection, Republic of Slovenia scholarship holders and exchange students. Citizens of non-EU countries with which the Republic of Slovenia has not signed a bilateral agreement, all part-time students, all doctoral students and all students holding an equivalent degree are obliged to pay. There is no application, no deadline, no competition, no stipend and no bond, and only the tuition fee is removed: enrolment fees and study contributions, health insurance, accommodation and living costs stay payable, so the award is not fully funded.
official.coverage: Tuition fee only, for full-time study, until the exemption conditions cease to apply. Enrolment fees and study contributions, compulsory health insurance, accommodation, living costs, study materials and travel are all outside the coverage.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your nationality or residence status appears in the University's fee-exempt list before you rely on this: EU plus Switzerland, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway; Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Serbia; permanent residence in Slovenia with tax residency; or international or temporary protection.
If you are a citizen of a non-EU country with no bilateral agreement with Slovenia, stop here: the University lists you among those obliged to pay, and this exemption is not available to you.
Enrol in full-time study only. Part-time enrolment puts you in the group the University lists as obliged to pay, and the exemption will not be applied.
Check you do not already hold an equivalent degree of education, which also puts you in the paying group.
Budget separately for everything the exemption does not touch: enrolment fee and study contributions, compulsory health insurance, accommodation and living costs, study materials and travel.
Open the price list for your own faculty or academy for the relevant academic year, rather than assuming the fee is the same across the University, and use that figure in your funding plan.

If you are changing study programme or direction, or re-enrolling in a programme you previously left, raise it with the enrolling faculty before enrolling, because both situations are listed as forfeiting the exemption.
Contact the University or the enrolling member institution in writing to have your exemption status confirmed for your specific nationality and residence combination before you commit funds.
If you already hold a Republic of Slovenia scholarship such as CMEPIUS or a JŠRIPSRS award, tell the enrolling institution, as scholarship holders are listed as fee-exempt.

Consider the Fund's separate state scholarship routes for non-EEA nationals, but note those are awarded by the Public Scholarship, Development, Disability and Maintenance Fund of the Republic of Slovenia and are outside this record
common_rejection_risks: Assuming this is an open scholarship anyone can apply for. It is a standing fee rule, so there is no application to submit and no outcome to be rejected from; if your nationality is not on the exempt list, the fee simply applies.
Enrolling part-time and losing the exemption without realising it, because the University lists all part-time students as obliged to pay.
Already holding an equivalent degree and therefore being liable for the full fee.
Changing study programme or direction and enrolling in the same or a lower study year after having repeated a year, which the University lists as forfeiting the exemption.
Re-enrolling in the same study programme or direction previously withdrawn from, which the University also lists as forfeiting the exemption.
Assuming the Western Balkans agreement extends to all non-EEA countries. The University names Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Serbia only.
Treating the exemption as fully funding the degree and being caught short on living costs in Ljubljana, which the fee waiver does nothing about.
Reading a third-party listing that calls this a 'Jasminka Scholarship'. No award of that name appears on the University of Ljubljana site.
Missing the annual change of fee tables and planning a budget from a previous academic year's per-faculty amount.
Assuming a state scholarship amount applies here. The Zois scholarships and the Fund's open calls named on the University page are awarded by the Fund, not the University.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs are the main gap. The exemption waives the tuition fee only and provides no stipend, so the full cost of living in Ljubljana, one of the more expensive capitals in the region, has to be met from other funds. No monthly figure is recorded in this record because the University's own cost-of-living guidance was not fetched; read the University international-students cost-of-living and accommodation pages, or your national scholarship body's published cost-of-living figure for Ljubljana, before budgeting.

Student dormitory rent or private rental, not covered. If you are not a Republic of Slovenia scholarship holder you do not have the subsidised scholarship-holder dormitory route described by the University, so expect the full foreign-student dormitory rate or market rent.
Compulsory health insurance for non-EU nationals, not covered by the fee exemption. Arrange it before the start of studies.

Enrolment fee and study contributions, charged separately from tuition and not covered, even where tuition is waived. Amounts are in the annual price list for enrolment fees and study contributions, which was not opened for this record.

Study materials, equipment and laboratory or fieldwork costs, depending on the faculty. The University's Heart UL campaign exists because enrolled students can face this kind of shortfall, which is why it is not safe to treat the fee waiver as complete funding.
Residence permit and visa costs, and health insurance required for the permit, for non-EU nationals.
Travel to and from Slovenia, which the exemption does not cover in either direction.

The tuition fee itself, for anyone outside the exempt categories, set per faculty and per study programme in the annual price lists. Those PDFs were not opened for this record, so no EUR figure is given here; use the figure for your own faculty.
Lost earnings or opportunity cost, which no fee exemption addresses and which applicants from outside the EEA should treat as a real component of the total cost.
document_audit: The University publishes no document checklist for this exemption, because there is no application. This list is derived guidance, not an official requirement.
Passport or other evidence of nationality, so the enrolling institution can check the fee-exempt nationality list, including the specific countries named under the bilateral agreements.

If you are a national of Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo or Serbia, the evidence relied on is the bilateral education agreement with the Republic of Slovenia, so confirm with the enrolling institution that it accepts your nationality at face value for fee purposes.
Evidence of permanent residence in the Republic of Slovenia together with tax residency, for you or for your parents or guardians, if you are claiming exemption on that ground.
Evidence of international protection or of temporary protection, if you are claiming exemption on that ground.
Evidence of a Republic of Slovenia scholarship such as CMEPIUS or a JŠRIPSRS award, if you are claiming exemption as a scholarship holder.
Evidence of exchange status, if you are claiming exemption as an exchange student.
Confirm you have no previously awarded equivalent degree, which the University treats as a disqualifying condition for the exemption.
Keep your enrolment confirmation showing full-time status, since the exemption depends on it and is easiest to verify when the faculty can see it at enrolment.
Keep the fee assessment or invoice from your faculty showing the tuition line at zero, so a later change of programme or re-enrolment can be checked against what you were actually charged.

alerts.message: If you are a citizen of a non-EU country with which Slovenia has no bilateral agreement, the University lists you as obliged to pay tuition fees and this exemption does not apply to you. Do not build a funding plan on it.
All part-time students are listed as obliged to pay tuition fees. Only full-time enrolment qualifies for the exemption, so switching to part-time mid-programme can create an immediate fee liability.

Changing programme or direction and enrolling in the same or a lower study year after repeating a year, or re-enrolling in a programme you withdrew from, are both listed as forfeiting the exemption. Clear this with the faculty before enrolling.

The University republishes tuition and study-contribution price lists each academic year, with a separate list per faculty. Never plan from a previous year's figure, and always use the list for your own faculty and programme.

This is a tuition reduction applied automatically on enrolment. There is no application window, no deadline, no shortlist and no award letter to wait for, and there is no application to submit before you enrol.

No 'Jasminka Scholarship' exists at the University of Ljubljana. The University's scholarships page names only the Residency of Prof. Grega Košak, the Heart UL campaign and state scholarships awarded by the Fund at srips-rs.si.

The Zois scholarships and the open calls for foreign nationals linked from the University page are awarded by the Public Scholarship, Development, Disability and Maintenance Fund of the Republic of Slovenia. Check that Fund's own call for deadlines and amounts; they are not covered by this record and are frequently restricted by nationality or to master's level.

submission_workflow: No application exists for this exemption, so there is nothing to submit and no submission deadline to track.

Apply and enrol in full-time study through the ordinary University of Ljubljana admission and enrolment route for your nationality, which for non-EU nationals runs through the published Call for Enrolment and is handled by the Higher Education Application and Information Service at vpis@uni-lj.si.
At enrolment, present the evidence for your fee-exempt nationality, residence or protection status to the enrolling member institution so that the tuition line is assessed at zero.
Check the tuition and study-contribution invoice issued at enrolment and confirm the tuition line is zero and that the remaining enrolment fee and study contributions are as you budgeted.
If the tuition line is not zero, take it up with the enrolling faculty immediately with your exemption evidence, since the exemption is applied at that point rather than awarded later.
Re-confirm full-time status and exemption eligibility at each annual re-enrolment, because the exemption is carried forward through enrolment and is lost if the study mode or the programme changes.
Arrange compulsory health insurance before the start of studies, and separately arrange a residence permit, as neither is included in the fee exemption.
Apply for dormitory accommodation early through the University or the student dormitory, and budget the foreign-student rate if you are not a Republic of Slovenia scholarship holder.

official.description: Middlebury College publishes no single named international scholarship; the funding it publishes for international undergraduates is need-based institutional financial aid. The College states that if you are an undergraduate student admitted to Middlebury it will meet your full demonstrated financial need, and that almost all of its financial aid is institutional grants and scholarships that do not have to be repaid. Its published figures are institutional rather than award-specific: $80M institutional aid awarded, 50% of students receiving financial aid, 100% calculated need met, a $66K average grant, and 100% need-based aid. For international applicants the College is need aware, so assistance must be requested when applying for admission and no later than the published deadlines, the CSS Profile is required for every prospective undergraduate applying for aid and must be submitted electronically for international students, and supporting parent tax forms or employer earning statements translated into English go through the College Board IDOC service. The College verifies the financial aid application of every undergraduate who enrolls and issues final offers in early summer. Aid includes all books and supplies, and higher-need students also qualify for student health insurance and a new laptop.
official.coverage: Full demonstrated financial need as calculated by the College for admitted undergraduates, covering tuition and the components included in the College's need calculation, with all books and supplies included and student health insurance and a laptop for higher-need students; travel is not listed as covered and no per-annum amount is published.

official.deadline_note: The binding date for this award is the Financial Aid Deadline, not the admissions deadline, because the CSS Profile and Certification of Finances must be submitted by it. The earliest financial aid deadline in the published table is 15 November 2026 for Early Decision I; the corresponding admissions deadlines are 1 November 2026 (ED I), 2 January 2027 (ED II and Regular Decision) and 1 March 2027 (transfer). official.funding_duration: Typically four years of undergraduate study. A need-based award made in the first year renews automatically in subsequent years without reapplication; the Hodson Trust Scholarship is described as renewable and the Charles R. official.tuition_coverage_note: For recipients, tuition is covered: Hopkins promises to meet 100% of a family's demonstrated need without any loans for international citizens admitted in Early Decision I, Early Decision II and Regular Decision, and publishes that families making up to $200,000 pay no tuition. fully_funded is nevertheless false because three limits remain. First, the award is need-based and selective: only about 10% of international students receive financial aid and merit scholarships to international citizens are a small number each year, so admission does not confer funding. Second, it meets demonstrated need rather than the full cost of attendance, so the family must still contribute what it can pay and the amount varies with need and can change year to year. Third, international students are ineligible for Title IV federal aid and state aid, so no federal or state grant can top up a shortfall, and work-study is a separate opportunity rather than part of this award.
