official.citizenship_residency: Open to applicants who are neither U.S. citizens nor permanent residents, eligible noncitizens, nor holders of DACA or undocumented status. Applicants holding an F-1, F-2, M-1, J-1, J-2, G-series, A-2/A-3, NATO, B-1/B-2, H-series, L-series or U visa, and who do not have DACA or undocumented status, are international applicants at Hopkins.
official.international_eligibility: International students are eligible for both need-based and merit scholarships, although Hopkins states both types of assistance are limited. Hopkins is need-aware for international students, meaning financial circumstances are considered in the admissions process, whereas it is need-blind for domestic applicants. For all international citizens admitted in Early Decision I, Early Decision II and Regular Decision, Hopkins promises to meet 100% of a family's demonstrated need without any loans, using need-based scholarships that do not need to be paid back. About 10% of international students receive financial aid, and a small number of merit scholarships are awarded to international citizens each year. All international applicants must submit the Certification of Finances; those seeking aid must also submit the CSS Profile. Hopkins does not currently offer financial aid to international transfer students, and international students are ineligible for federal and state aid.
official.application_method: Merit scholarships are automatic on admission: every applicant is automatically considered for merit scholarships when applying, no separate application is required, and recipients are notified at the time of the admissions decision. Need-based aid requires a separate, mandatory financial aid step: the applicant must indicate an interest in financial aid on the admissions application and submit the International Student Certification of Finances plus the CSS Profile (or the free JHU ISFAA alternative) by the financial aid deadline of the chosen admissions plan. There is no separate application for international applicants beyond the standard admissions application, and international students cannot apply for financial aid after admissions decisions are released.
official.application_route: Undergraduate Admissions application submitted through the Common Application or Coalition on Scoir, plus the Hopkins applicant portal for the International Student Certification of Finances, and the CSS Profile through the College Board or the free Johns Hopkins University International Student Financial Aid Application alternative form.

official.description: Johns Hopkins University is need-aware for international students and promises to meet 100% of a family's demonstrated need without any loans for international citizens admitted in Early Decision I, Early Decision II and Regular Decision, using need-based scholarships that do not need to be paid back. About 10% of international students receive financial aid. Hopkins also awards a small number of merit scholarships each year on academic and personal achievement, for which international citizens are eligible in all admissions plans and are automatically considered with no separate application. Need-based aid requires the applicant to indicate an interest in financial aid on the admissions application and to submit the CSS Profile and International Student Certification of Finances by the financial aid deadline.

official.coverage: Meets 100% of a family's demonstrated need, defined as the difference between the total cost of attendance each year and what a family can pay, without any loans and using grants that do not need to be paid back. The award amount varies with financial need and can change year to year if household or financial circumstances change. Hopkins also states that families making up to $200,000 pay no tuition. Federal Pell, FSEOG and state aid are listed on the same pages but are FAFSA-based and unavailable to international students, and work-study is a separate opportunity.

official.description: Southern Methodist University in Dallas, Texas automatically considers every applicant, regardless of citizenship, for its academic merit scholarships as part of the undergraduate admission application; SMU states there is no separate application process. International applicants are eligible on the same nationality basis as everyone else, but need-based financial aid is closed to them and is available only to U.S. citizens and permanent U.S. residents. The merit family comprises the President's Scholarship (full tuition and fees, one study abroad experience, and a housing scholarship for on-campus students), the Nancy Ann and Ray L. Hunt Leadership Scholarship (about 75 percent of tuition and fees plus a study abroad experience), the Provost, SMU Distinguished, Second Century and University Scholarships (partial or full tuition), the International Baccalaureate Scholarship (USD 7,500 per academic year), the Dallas County Promise Scholarship, the Mustang Scholarship and the Robert H. Dedman SMU Scholarship. Most awards are stackable but the combined total cannot exceed the cost of tuition and fees, so none of them is a complete cost-of-study package.
official.coverage: Merit tuition assistance only, capped at the cost of tuition and fees. Named award values range from USD 7,500 per academic year to full tuition and fees. Room and board is covered only under the President's Scholarship housing scholarship for on-campus students, and only that award plus the Mustang and Dedman awards include housing. Living expenses, travel, visa and I-20 issuance costs, insurance and health costs are not covered by any of these awards.

official.description: The Dean's International Award Program is Queen's University Kingston's automatic admission-award programme for international students entering the first year of a first-entry undergraduate degree programme in the Faculty of Arts and Science, the Smith School of Business (Bachelor of Commerce), the Stephen J. R. Smith School of Engineering and Applied Science, or the Faculty of Health Sciences (Bachelor of Health Sciences). It comprises four faculty awards - Arts and Science, Commerce, Engineering and Health Sciences International Admission Awards - published at CAD 5,000, 10,000, 15,000, 20,000 or 25,000 per year, with a four-year duration renewable for three subsequent years while the student stays registered full-time in a programme within the original faculty of admission. The award is a partial tuition-side award and does not cover living costs, ancillary fees or travel.

official.description: The Welcome to Canada Admission Scholarship is offered by Western University's Office of the Registrar as an unlimited number of awards for international students entering full-time first-year studies at Western's main campus. Each award provides CAD 10,000 for the first year and a guaranteed place in on-campus residence for the first two years of study. Consideration is automatic with the admission application and there is no separate application, no published academic-average threshold and no published selection weighting. The award cannot be combined with any other admission scholarship, although the New to Canada Grant is payable on top of it. It is not a tuition waiver: Western publishes an estimated year 1 international tuition and fees range of CAD 48,000 to 64,400.

official.application_cycle: Automatic admission-linked award for Fall entry each year. Brock publishes the international amount table on its 2026-2027 international students page, so the currently published tiers are the 2026 entry figures and are 'subject to annual approval by the Board of Trustees and are subject to change'. There is no scholarship application cycle because no application is required.
official.deadline_central_display: No separate scholarship deadline. The award is 'offered at the time of admission'. To keep it, the student must 'Reply to your offer of admission by the deadline specified by the Registrar's Office'.
official.deadline_note: No exact calendar date is published for this award and none has been invented. Brock publishes no scholarship application deadline because there is no scholarship application: the award is automatic and 'offered at the time of admission'. The only date-bearing instruction in the published terms is the confirmation requirement to 'Reply to your offer of admission by the deadline specified by the Registrar's Office', and Brock does not publish that date on the scholarship pages; it is programme- and term-specific and is published by the Registrar's Office. A related hard date is published for transcripts rather than for the award: Brock states that official transcripts 'will only be accepted until Oct. 31' for scholarship revisions.
official.status_note: The award is open because it has no application window to close: Brock states the awards are 'open to every incoming student from anywhere in the world' and that 'No application is required'. At the verification date of 2026-10-03 Brock's published amount tables are the 2026-2027 entry figures, and the page footer carries a 2026 copyright. The one separate-application international award on the same page, the International Ambassador Award, is marked '2026 Application Closed', which confirms that the automatic award itself remains open for current applicants.
official.funding_duration: Renewable. Three renewals in a four-year honours degree (maximum four years of funding in total) or two renewals in a three-year pass degree.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The award is applied against tuition, not paid as an unrestricted stipend. Brock states that the award 'currently includes a renewable financial component to partially offset tuition fees' and that 'Your scholarship will be applied directly to your tuition fees. This will take place before classes begin in September, reducing the amount you owe to the University.' tuition_coverage is therefore true in the sense that the money directly reduces tuition. However the University explicitly calls it a partial offset, the published maximum of CAD $32,000 is a fraction of a full international tuition load, and no tuition-fee waiver, living-cost, residence or travel component is published, so fully_funded is false. Two published limits apply: scholarships 'cannot be used for first instalments or down payments', and 'students already holding a tuition waiver will have the academic distinction noted on their transcript but will not receive the tuition offset funding'.
official.funding_label: Automatic entrance award for incoming international undergraduates, tiered by final admission average: up to CAD $32,000 in year 1 and CAD $20,000 per renewal at 95.0 per cent and above, CAD $24,000 and CAD $15,000 at 90.0-94.9 per cent, CAD $12,500 and CAD $8,000 at 85.0-89.9 per cent, CAD $7,000 and CAD $4,000 at 80.0-84.9 per cent. Applied directly against tuition as a partial offset; renewable for up to three further years. Not full funding, and no living-cost component is published.

official.description: The International Brock Scholars Award is Brock University's largest award and its automatic entrance award for students from outside Canada. Brock states that it is 'open to every incoming student from anywhere in the world', requiring only that the student be entering their first undergraduate programme in the Fall term with no previous post-secondary experience, and that 'No application is required'. The award is an academic distinction based on final admission average and carries a renewable financial component that partially offsets tuition fees and is applied directly against them before classes begin in September. Published 2026 first-year amounts range from CAD $7,000 to CAD $32,000, with renewal amounts from CAD $4,000 to CAD $20,000. Award amounts are subject to annual approval by the Board of Trustees and are subject to change.
official.coverage: A renewable tuition offset for incoming international undergraduates, tiered by final admission average: first-year amounts of CAD $32,000, CAD $24,000, CAD $12,500 or CAD $7,000, and renewal amounts of CAD $20,000, CAD $15,000, CAD $8,000 or CAD $4,000. The money is applied directly to tuition fees. It is explicitly a partial offset rather than full tuition, and no living-cost, residence, meal, travel or health component is published for this award.

application_readiness_checklist: Do not look for a scholarship form. This award is automatic: Brock states 'No application is required', so the only thing you submit is an undergraduate admission application as an international fee-paying student

Aim for a final admission average of at least 80 per cent, because below that 'you will no longer be eligible for a Brock Scholars award'; the tiers at 95.0 and above, 90.0-94.9, 85.0-89.9 and 80.0-84.9 are worth very different amounts
Make sure you are entering your first undergraduate programme in the Fall term with no previous post-secondary experience, since both conditions are required to qualify
If you are applying from the United States, check the domestic award instead; Brock states 'U.S.A. applicants will only qualify for Domestic Brock Scholars Award amounts'
If you already hold a Brock tuition waiver, understand that you receive the academic distinction but not the tuition offset funding, because Brock states those two are mutually exclusive

Reply to your offer of admission by the Registrar's Office deadline, since confirming the scholarship requires it alongside the name, programme, year of study and likeness release, and full-time registration
Register a full-time course load of at least 1.50 credits in each of the Fall and Winter terms, because reducing to part-time pro-rates or withdraws the award
Watch the transcript cut-off. Brock states official transcripts 'will only be accepted until Oct. 31' for scholarship revisions, and summer courses taken after graduation will be used in the revision

If you are a co-op student, complete the Brock Scholars Award Renewal Form so that your renewal is reviewed, and note that work-term additive credit courses used for the co-op certification are excluded from the milestone calculation
If you are in a three-year pass degree, plan for two renewals rather than three; honours degrees of four years get three
If you intend to apply for OSAP, do not list this scholarship under Award Income in the OSAP application, because Brock reports it on your behalf
common_rejection_risks: Hunting for a scholarship application that does not exist and assuming there is a deadline to meet; this award requires no application at all
A final admission average below 80 per cent, which ends eligibility entirely rather than reducing the tier
A final average that lands below the band offered on the provisional offer, because Brock states the award 'may increase or decrease if your final average changes'
Applicants with previous post-secondary experience, who are excluded because the award requires entering a first undergraduate programme
Applying from the USA and expecting the international tiers, which Brock says are unavailable to USA applicants
Missing the Registrar's Office reply deadline for the admission offer, which is the only step that confirms the scholarship
Dropping below a full-time course load, which causes the tuition offset or scholarship to be pro-rated or withdrawn
Falling under 80 per cent in a 5.0 credit milestone and losing the renewal
Expecting the award to pay living costs, housing or travel; it is a tuition-only partial offset
Relying on it to cover a first instalment or down payment, which Brock explicitly excludes
estimated_uncovered_costs: The majority of international tuition fees. Even the top tier of CAD $32,000 in year 1 is only a partial offset and the University describes it as 'a renewable financial component to partially offset tuition fees'
All renewal tuition above CAD $20,000 per year at the top tier, and above CAD $15,000, CAD $8,000 or CAD $4,000 at the lower tiers
Non-instructional and other program-related fees; the award is applied to tuition and no separate fee coverage is published
Residence and meal plan costs, for which no coverage is published on the award page
Books and supplies

Health insurance. Brock publishes Universal Health Insurance Plan (UHIP) as mandatory health insurance coverage for all international students, plus a BUSU Health and Dental Plan described as a mandatory fee for all international students, and an International recovery fee of CAD $750 charged by the Province of Ontario to all international students at public colleges and universities
Any tuition instalment or down payment, which the scholarship cannot be used for
Study permit fees, travel to Canada and other arrival costs not named in the published provision

official.application_cycle: Annual, aligned to entry term. The published cycle statement is: "The 2027-2028 General Entrance Award program opens on October 1, 2026, with an application deadline of February 15, 2027." A separate early-entrance track exists with its own acceptance date, January 31, at which point an early award offer must be accepted by paying the admission deposit.
official.deadline_central_display: February 15. Published as "an application deadline of February 15, 2027" for the 2027-2028 General Entrance Award program, and repeated for international undergraduates on the Info for International Students page: "GEA is applicable to students coming direct from high school if you apply by February 15."
official.deadline_note: The date is confirmed exactly as published by Dalhousie on both official pages fetched; no time of day is published on either, so deadline_central_timezone is null rather than assumed. Dalhousie's deadlines would fall in America/Halifax (Atlantic Standard Time in February), but no published time was read, so no clock time or timezone is claimed. deadline_institutional is null because there is no separate institutional round: one central GEA deadline governs the programme. Secondary dates recorded separately and not treated as the programme deadline: January 31 for accepting an early entrance award offer by paying the admission deposit, and March 1 for the small set of awards requiring a separate application (Fountain Performing Arts Undergraduate Scholarships, Harrison McCain Scholarships, Bachelor of Computer Science and Bachelor of Applied Computer Science Entrance Scholarships, Leacross Women in Technology Entrance Scholarship), all of which are separate applications outside the single GEA route.
official.status_note: Open at the time of verification on 2026-10-03. The published 2027-2028 cycle opened on October 1, 2026, two days before verification, and does not close until February 15, 2027, so the window is live and not yet closed. Dalhousie reviews applications after the February 15 deadline and notifies successful applicants in the spring. Status refers to the single current GEA cycle; no past cycle is represented in this record.
official.funding_period: One-time, or renewable for up to 4 years.
official.funding_duration: Awards may be one-time or renewable for up to 4 years. Dalhousie publishes an approximate yearly value range of "$1K to $80K" for entrance awards and states they can run "over 4 years"; named international awards are quoted per year with renewal, for example the Murray Family Jamaican Engineering Scholarship at "$88,000 ($22,000 renewable for 4 years)" and the international Sankofa Scholarships at "$48,000 ($12,000 per year renewable for 4 years)".
official.tuition_coverage_note: Not a tuition waiver and not a tuition reduction. Awards are applied to the student account in two equal instalments in mid-August and mid-December, and any money remaining after tuition and fees are paid may be refunded to the student. The tuition fee itself remains payable and is offset by the award credit; Dalhousie's International Tuition Guarantee fixes and guarantees the fee for the standard programme length rather than covering it, and the guarantee lists only the Faculties of Agriculture, Arts & Social Sciences, Computer Science, Engineering, Management and Science, so it is narrower than the set of undergraduate awards. Because the programme leaves tuition payable and publishes no tuition-waiver component, tuition_coverage is false and fully_funded is false.
official.funding_label: Entrance award credit against the student account, in the approximate range of $1K to $80K per year for the 2,000+ awards offered annually, one-time or renewable for up to 4 years. Tuition and fees remain payable and are offset by the credit; no published guaranteed living-cost, travel, visa or accommodation component, and no bond, service obligation or repayment clause published.

official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship, residency or international-status test is published for the programme as a whole. Dalhousie states flatly that "All students—domestic and international—are eligible to apply", and instructs international students to consider entrance awards "by submitting the General Entrance Award application". Individual named awards carry their own residency or nationality conditions, and several awards listed elsewhere on the same page are restricted to Canadian citizens, permanent residents or Canadian high school graduates and so are closed to an international applicant.
official.international_eligibility: Confirmed directly and explicitly. The Info for International Students page states that "Dalhousie offers more than 2,000 entrance awards (scholarships) each year, including scholarships and bursaries to support incoming students", that "Awards may be offered based on academics, achievements and involvement outside of the classroom, financial need or a combination of the above", and that "A general entrance award application is required to be considered". Its step-by-step international undergraduate pathway includes step 3, "Apply for scholarships: Take advantage of funding opportunities to support your studies by submitting your application for General Entrance Awards (GEA) through your Application Portal", with the note "GEA is applicable to students coming direct from high school if you apply by February 15." The Future undergraduate student awards page carries a dedicated "International students" section: "International students are considered for entrance awards by submitting the General Entrance Award application." International-specific documents are also addressed: a non-Canadian curriculum still requires Grade 12 first-semester marks, and where an Income Tax Notice of Assessment is unavailable, official government tax or income documents from the home country showing parent or guardian income, or an official employer letter, are accepted, with an English translation required if not in English or French. Several awards on the page are explicitly open only to Canadian students and do not reach an international applicant: Schulich Leader Scholarships (Canadian high school or CEGEP graduate and Canadian citizen), Harrison McCain Scholarships (Canadian citizens or permanent residents) and the Bissett Scholarship (Cole Harbour High School applicants). The Leacross Women in Technology Entrance Scholarship is explicitly open to "Canadian and international applicants".
official.study_mode: Full-time enrolment required to be paid: the award is applied only in the terms in which the student is "registered full-time (minimum 9 credit hours per term for degree students and 6 credit hours per term for technology students) at Dalhousie University for the term(s) in which the scholarship is awarded". The page publishes no part-time award route for the GEA programme.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field or subject restriction at programme level: one GEA application considers the applicant across faculties and programmes. Named awards are programme-restricted, including Bachelor of Commerce (CorpFinance Indian Scholarship), Bachelor of Engineering with preference for Civil Engineering (Murray Family Jamaican Engineering Scholarship), Bachelor of Computer Science and Bachelor of Applied Computer Science (WeAreAllCS awards, Bachelor of Computer Science entrance scholarships, Leacross Women in Technology Entrance Scholarship), Bachelor of Commerce and Bachelor of Management (Faculty of Management Promise Scholarship for Black and Indigenous Students), Music and Theatre (Fountain Performing Arts Undergraduate Scholarships), and Architecture & Planning, Arts & Social Sciences, Computer Science, Engineering, Health and Management (Bissett Scholarship, which is also restricted to Cole Harbour High School applicants). Athletic scholarships are handled separately by Dalhousie Athletics via a prospective recruit form or direct contact with a coach. The International Tuition Guarantee, which fixes rather than funds tuition, covers only the Faculties of Agriculture, Arts & Social Sciences, Computer Science, Engineering, Management and Science.
official.application_method: One General Entrance Award application, submitted by the applicant through the Dalhousie application portal at https://apply.dal.ca/apply/ after the admission application. If already accepted: complete the GEA application in the portal and submit an official first-semester transcript or provincial student ID number. If not yet accepted: apply to an undergraduate programme, complete the GEA application, pay the $70 CAD admissions application fee, and submit an official first-semester transcript or provincial student ID number. Applicants admitted on self-reported grades must additionally submit an official record of first-semester results. Financial or disability-related supporting documents are uploaded directly into the GEA application in the portal.
official.application_route: Dalhousie application portal (https://apply.dal.ca/apply/) for both the admission application and the General Entrance Award application. Transcripts must be sent by the school or issuing institution directly to admissions.documents@dal.ca to be considered official. A small number of awards require a separate application through their own route (Schulich Leader Scholarships programme, the Fountain School of Performing Arts, the Faculty of Computer Science, an external Microsoft Forms page for Harrison McCain, the Cole Harbour High guidance office, or Dalhousie Athletics), but the international-student awards named on the page are reached through the single GEA application.

official.description: Dalhousie University's General Entrance Award program (GEA) is the single undergraduate entrance award route through which international students are considered for scholarships, bursaries and hybrid merit-and-need awards, and one of the 2,000+ entrance awards offered annually at an approximate yearly value range of $1K to $80K, one-time or renewable for up to 4 years. One application places the applicant in the pool for hundreds of awards, assessed individually on academic achievement, leadership and initiative, extracurricular involvement, community service, financial need and cultural identity, on the basis of Grade 12 first-semester final grades. Eligibility is open to domestic and international students alike, requires applying directly from high school or being a mature student with no transferable post-secondary study, requires Fall entry and the usual academic threshold, and excludes transfer students. The published cycle opened on October 1, 2026 and closes February 15, 2027. Awards are credited to the student account in two instalments in mid-August and mid-December against tuition and fees, with any residual refundable; tuition is not waived, there is no bond, and living, travel and immigration costs are not covered as published components.
official.coverage: A monetary award credit applied to the student account against tuition and fees in two equal instalments (mid-August, mid-December), one-time or renewable for up to 4 years, with residual funds over tuition and fees refundable. Not covered: any tuition waiver, a guaranteed living-cost component, residence and meal plan costs beyond residual credit, travel, study permit, eTA, visa and Provincial Attestation Letter costs.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are starting in the Fall term. Winter and Summer entry cannot use the GEA route; Dalhousie directs those students to current undergraduate student awards and bursaries instead.

Confirm you are applying directly from high school, or that you qualify as a mature student with no transferable post-secondary study. Transfer students are generally not eligible, and the only stated exception is Indigenous Black and First Nations students from the Maritimes seeking the FNIB Scholarship.
Check the cycle is live: the 2027-2028 GEA program opened October 1, 2026 and the deadline is February 15, 2027.
Have your Grade 12 first-semester final grades ready. If your school does not use semesters, first-half-of-year predicted or mid-term grades are acceptable.

Ask your school or issuing institution to send the transcript directly to admissions.documents@dal.ca. A transcript you upload yourself is not treated as official, and awards are not reassessed on later grades.

If your OUAC number or Nova Scotia Student ID number is already on file with Admissions you usually do not need to resend the transcript; check whether it already appears on your admission application status page, which is where transcripts are displayed, not in DalOnline.

If you have not yet been accepted: apply to an undergraduate programme and pay the $70 CAD admissions application fee as part of the award process. If you were admitted on self-reported grades, submit an official record of your first-semester results, because self-reported grades alone are not considered for the GEA programme.
Do not prepare reference letters, a resume, SAT/ACT scores or IELTS scores for the GEA application. None are required, and reference letters are not accepted for this programme.

If you need need-based support, upload financial or disability-related documents directly into the GEA application in the portal. Where an Income Tax Notice of Assessment is unavailable, use official government tax or income documents from your home country showing your parent or guardian income, or an official employer letter, with an English translation if not in English or French.

Review which of your awards are actually open to you. Schulich Leader Scholarships, Harrison McCain Scholarships and the Bissett Scholarship are closed to international applicants, and most separate-application awards are limited to students entering directly from Canadian high schools.

Plan the payment mechanics: the award lands on your student account in two equal instalments in mid-August and mid-December, and only registered full-time students (9 credit hours per term, 6 for technology) receive it.
If you are offered an early entrance award, be ready to pay your admission deposit by January 31 to lock it in.
common_rejection_risks: Missing the February 15 deadline. Dalhousie reviews applications after that date and gives no extension, and the date is fixed regardless of when the admission application was submitted.
Applying on self-reported grades only. Dalhousie states self-reported grades alone are not considered for the GEA programme, and awards are decided on Grade 12 first-semester final grades.
Uploading your own transcript instead of having the school send it to admissions.documents@dal.ca, which means it is not considered official.
Holding transferable post-secondary study. Transfer students are generally not eligible, and this cannot be waived after the fact.
Applying for Winter or Summer entry and assuming the GEA applies. Those intakes are directed to current student awards and bursaries.

Expecting IELTS or other language scores to improve the award outcome. The GEA application uses only the information in the GEA application, and IELTS scores are neither required nor considered for it.

Assuming an award title on a third-party listing is open to international applicants. Schulich Leader Scholarships, Harrison McCain Scholarships and the Bissett Scholarship all carry Canadian residency or school conditions.
Dropping below full-time enrolment. The award is only applied in terms in which you are registered full-time, so a lighter course load silently stops the payment.
Assuming the award waives tuition. It does not: the credit is applied against tuition and fees and the fee stays payable, so a shortfall against the full international fee is still yours to cover.
Double-counting a GEA alongside an Early Entrance Scholarship. Dalhousie keeps the higher-value award only.

Deferring admission without checking the rules. Deferral is limited to the winter term and requires an approved admission deferral, and completing transferable post-secondary study during the deferred year forfeits eligibility to re-apply.
Planning around a specific award amount. Dalhousie publishes only a $1K to $80K approximate range across 2,000+ awards, so no named amount should be relied on in a funding plan.
estimated_uncovered_costs: The tuition fee itself. Awards are credits applied to the student account, not a waiver, so the full international tuition fee remains payable and must be met by the award plus other funds. Dalhousie's International Tuition Guarantee fixes and guarantees the fee for the standard programme length rather than covering it, and only for the Faculties of Agriculture, Arts & Social Sciences, Computer Science, Engineering, Management and Science. No tuition figure is recorded here because the tuition and fee calculator and tuition page were not fetched for this record.

Room and board. Residence is a separate charge and the page publishes no housing component of the award. An award that exceeds tuition and fees leaves a residual that is refunded, but that depends on the award size and is not a guaranteed living-cost amount.
Provincial Attestation Letter, study permit, Temporary Resident Visa and eTA fees for international students, none of which is listed as an award benefit.
Books, equipment and course materials. Dalhousie itself points students with urgent textbook costs toward an emergency loan, which indicates these costs are normally self-funded.

alerts.message: The 2027-2028 General Entrance Award program closed its window on February 15, 2027. Dalhousie reviews applications after that date and notifies successful applicants in the spring, so a late application cannot be salvaged by an earlier admission submission.

If you were admitted using self-reported grades, Dalhousie states applications with self-reported grades alone will not be considered for the General Entrance Award program. You must submit an official record of your first-semester results.

Transfer students are generally not eligible for entrance awards, and the only stated exception is Indigenous Black and First Nations students from the Maritimes seeking the FNIB Scholarship. Holding transferable post-secondary study also ends any eligibility to re-apply after deferring.
The GEA route is Fall entry only. Students starting in winter or summer are directed to current undergraduate student awards and bursaries instead, which are a different pool with different terms.

Funds are applied only in terms in which you are registered full-time, a minimum of 9 credit hours per term for degree students or 6 credit hours per term for technology students. Reducing your course load silently stops the award for that term.

alerts.trigger: An award title that looks international but is not
alerts.message: Schulich Leader Scholarships require a Canadian high school or CEGEP graduation and Canadian citizenship, Harrison McCain Scholarships require Canadian citizenship or permanent residency, and the Bissett Scholarship is restricted to Cole Harbour High School applicants. Check the eligibility line on each award before planning around it.

This is an account credit against tuition and fees, not a fee waiver, and the International Tuition Guarantee only fixes the fee at a guaranteed level for six named faculties. Budget the full international fee and treat the award as an offset.

If you hold both a General Entrance Award and an Early Entrance Scholarship, Dalhousie keeps only the higher-value award. Early offers must be accepted by paying the admission deposit by January 31, and that guarantees no less than the early award amount.

alerts.trigger: Timing pressure after the award offer
alerts.message: After paying the admission deposit you receive a Provincial Attestation Letter that must be used for your study permit within 12 weeks. Build the immigration timeline backwards from the February 15 award deadline and the spring notification, not forwards from it.

submission_workflow: Submit your undergraduate admission application through the application portal at https://apply.dal.ca/apply/, paying the $70 CAD admissions application fee if you have not already paid one.
Complete the General Entrance Award application yourself in the same application portal. This single application is what puts you forward for hundreds of awards.
Ask your school or issuing institution to transmit your official Grade 12 first-semester transcript directly to admissions.documents@dal.ca. Do not rely on a self-uploaded copy.

Upload any financial or disability-related supporting documents directly inside the GEA application in the portal, and use home-country government income documents or an employer letter with an English translation if you have no Income Tax Notice of Assessment.
Verify everything is in before the February 15, 2027 deadline: Dalhousie states you must complete the application and submit all required documents before the deadline, and reviews only after it.
After the deadline, wait for notification in the spring; there is no published appeal process.
If you hold an early entrance award offer, pay your admission deposit by January 31 to guarantee no less than that early amount.
Accept your offer of admission and pay the deposit through the portal to secure the award, then expect the credit on your student account in two equal instalments in mid-August and mid-December.
Keep enrolment at full-time load every term the award is paid, so the 9 credit hour (or 6, technology) requirement is met and no instalment is withheld.

After the last day to add classes in each term, check whether a residual balance remains and request a refund from Student Accounts if you want the money sooner than term end; for urgent costs such as textbooks in the meantime, apply for an emergency loan.

official.description: The President's International Entrance Scholarship is the University of Guelph's flagship automatic-on-admission international entrance award. U of G states that international students can 'Earn up to $42,500 CAD in international entrance scholarships over four years!' and that these awards are 'Receive a guaranteed entrance scholarship based on your admission average, payable over four years. No scholarship application is required, with eligible students being notified through their offer of admission.' For the 2027 entry cycle, year 1 is banded from $10,000 (70.0-84.9% admission average) to $20,000 (95.0%+) and years 2-4 pay $7,500 per year, giving four-year totals from $32,500 to $42,500 CAD. The award is limited to international applicants paying international tuition who are entering semester one of any degree program and have not previously attended post-secondary study. It is a partial award: recipients must continue to pay international tuition and fees.
official.program_type: University merit scholarship (international entrance, automatic on admission)
official.coverage: Tuition-fee credit applied to the University of Guelph student account in two equal payments over the fall and winter semesters, with conditional renewal in years 2-4. No living-cost, travel or health-insurance coverage.

application_readiness_checklist: Apply to the University of Guelph through the international undergraduate admission application and complete every item Admission Services requests.
Send the curriculum-specific supporting documentation for your education system early; the scholarship decision is triggered when Admission Services has received it, not when you apply.

Check your admission average against the published bands (70.0-84.9%, 85.0-89.9%, 90.0-94.9%, 95.0%+) and aim for the top band, since each band step changes both the year 1 amount and the four-year total.
Read the offer of admission carefully: the scholarship is announced with the offer, so there is nothing separate to submit afterwards.
If you miss the band on your first offer, remember the University re-considered in May and August, so keep your marks up in later terms.
Budget for the international difference: the award is applied to your student account as tuition credit but does not remove the requirement to pay international tuition and fees.
If you are transferring rather than entering from high school, check the separate International Transfer Scholarship instead; the transfer route is not covered by this award.
Use the Undergraduate Award Search to see whether additional awards in your program or college stack with this one.
common_rejection_risks: Deferring the offer of admission: entrance scholarships cannot be deferred, and the deferred applicant is only reconsidered the following year based on availability.
Falling below the 80.0% renewal average in a full-time year, which cancels years 2-4; lost payments cannot be added to the end of the award period.
Dropping below full-time registration in either the fall or winter semester, which reduces or cancels the award value.
Paying domestic tuition and fees after the offer, which downgrades the award to the domestic University of Guelph Entrance Scholarship (E0291) values.
Having previous post-secondary study: the award requires that the applicant has not attended a post-secondary institution.
Incomplete supporting documentation, so Admission Services never triggers the scholarship consideration.
Assuming a March 8, 2027 deadline applies here; that date is for the Dr. Franco J. Vaccarino President's Scholarship only, and missing it forfeits that separate $42,500 award.
Planning a major or college change that breaks a related college-specific international Dean's award renewal condition.

alerts.message: There is no scholarship application, no deadline and no award letter to wait for. The University states the awards to entering undergraduates "are made at the time of admission. No additional application is required." Focus on the admission intake, not on a scholarship round.

alerts.trigger: Admission does not guarantee the award
alerts.message: The University states the awards are made at the time of admission, but it does not state that all admitted international undergraduates receive one. Treat the award as conditional on the admission decision rather than automatic with the offer.

No monetary value for this award was read from an official page during this research, and this record therefore carries nulls where an amount would normally appear. Do not budget against a figure from a third-party listing; check the University's current entrance awards regulations for the year of entry.

This is an entrance award for entering undergraduates. If you are already studying at Windsor, the University directs continuing students to in-course awards and bursaries instead, which are separate awards with their own published values.

alerts.trigger: Government-sponsored aid is closed to internationals
alerts.message: The University states that government sponsored financial aid is not available to international students, and that students must be Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents or considered a Protected Person of Canada. Do not build a funding plan on government-sponsored aid as an international student.

alerts.trigger: Study in Canada is a separate track
alerts.message: The University states the Study in Canada Scholarship is provided by Global Affairs Canada but requires the University of Windsor to submit an application on your behalf. It is a different award with a different route, and this record does not cover it.

The domestic Open Entrance table shows Blue and Gold $1,000, Dean's $10,000 and President's $16,000, but that programme is open to domestic students only from 2026-27. International applicants are assessed on the Global Lancer scale of $4,000 to $24,000 over four years.
The minimum scholarship average is 85% at the end of each 2-term study period, not an 80% threshold as with some other Canadian entrants awards.

alerts.trigger: Co-op courses are excluded from the average
alerts.message: The admission average uses the top 6 Grade 12 U or M level qualifying courses and explicitly excludes co-op courses.
The May scholarship offer only changes if the admission average rises on courses completed by June 30.

alerts.trigger: Payments are instalments against your account
alerts.message: Value appears as Anticipated Aid before the term fee deadline of August 15 for Fall, December 15 for Winter and May 15 for Summer, and is paid after each semester drop date.

submission_workflow: No submission step exists for this award, because the University states no additional application is required.
Apply for admission to the University of Windsor as an international student through the University's normal undergraduate admission route for the year you intend to enter.
Submit the strong academic record the admission assessment relies on, since the University states the awards recognise academic achievement.
Read your admission offer carefully to see whether an award has been attached, as the University states these awards are made at the time of admission.
If an award is attached, check the terms attached to it before accepting, because the University's entrance awards regulations set the conditions students must continue to meet.

After enrolment, check your student account each term to confirm the award is credited, since the University states most awards are credited a term at a time and appear as anticipated aid before the term fee deadline date.
Keep your cumulative average and course load at the levels the award terms require, because failure to meet renewal requirements removes eligibility on a term-by-term basis.
